text: An 8-bit unsigned counter is a ring of 256 patterns. Add 1 at 255 and it wraps to 0. C defines this for unsigned types.
The same patterns can be read as signed numbers. In two's complement the top bit is worth minus 128, so 1111 1011 is minus 5, not 251.
Unsigned char 250 plus 10 wraps to 4. Adding 1 to the largest signed int is undefined behaviour: the browser's checker reports it instead of wrapping.
